idea.name: problem
idea.description: The specific problem it solves, and for whom. Concrete beats broad.
idea.example: designers hand a design system to an AI coding agent and get back code that ignores it

idea.name: audience
idea.description: The first users, narrowly. Not "everyone who ..." — the ten people who would use it this month.
idea.example: designers who already keep a DESIGN.md and work with coding agents daily

idea.name: solution
idea.description: What would actually be built or made, in one or two sentences.
idea.example: a gallery of DESIGN.md files rendered live, with a validator, a token lab and a merge tool

idea.name: why_now
idea.description: What changed recently — technology, rules, behavior — that makes this newly possible or newly needed. The single fact most often left out.
idea.example: Google Labs published an open DESIGN.md spec and coding agents now read design files directly

idea.name: monetization
idea.description: How it would make money, or that it is deliberately not meant to.
idea.example: free gallery, paid team workspace for shared systems

idea.name: competitors_known
idea.description: What people use today instead — named alternatives, or how they cope without one.
idea.example: getdesign.md, Refero Styles, design.dev's token editor; most people just paste tokens into the prompt

idea.name: differentiation
idea.description: The one thing this does that the existing options do not.
idea.example: one page re-skinned by the file itself, so the demo is the product

profile.name: background
profile.description: Your relationship to this idea — what you have built, what you know, whether you have the problem yourself. Without it, founder-fit questions are left unscored rather than guessed.
profile.example: solo dev, ten years in design tooling, I hit this every week

profile.name: skills
profile.description: What you can build or do yourself.
profile.example: Go, SvelteKit, enough design to ship it alone

profile.name: domains
profile.description: Fields you know from the inside.

profile.name: network
profile.description: Who you can already reach — users, buyers, distribution.
profile.example: 4k followers who are mostly designers; two agency friends who would pilot it

profile.name: would_use_myself
profile.description: Whether you would use the finished thing yourself, and how often.
profile.example: yes, on every project I start

profile.name: time_horizon
profile.description: How much time you actually have for this.
profile.example: evenings and weekends for about three months
